body:
**Partly false alarm: Eternal (Zomato) losses, dilution and a 700x P/E** (`case_study:false-alarm-eternal-zomato-losses-dilution`, verified). FLAGS: losses every year to FY23 (cumulative ~-Rs 7,450 cr FY15-23); OPM -17% to -252%; shares issued for Blinkit (2022) and a Rs 8,500 cr QIP at Rs 252.62 (Nov 2024), equity capital Rs 764 cr -> Rs 921 cr (~+20% shares, plus ESOPs); after profits came, OPM only 2-3% and P/E ~712 (Nov 2026). CONTEXT: (1) food delivery's contribution margin turned positive before reported profits did, so losses were spend on growth and quick commerce; (2) the 2024 QIP was raised near highs, from domestic MFs, to fund dark stores, not to survive; (3) the low OPM in FY26 is partly an accounting change: Blinkit's move to an inventory-led model books the full value of goods as revenue (consolidated sales jumped to Rs 54,364 cr in FY26), which mechanically shrinks margin %. Stock: IPO Rs 76 (Jul 2021) -> low ~Rs 47 (2022) -> Rs 364 (20 Nov 2026), ~7.8x from the low. HONEST CAVEAT: at P/E ~700 the stock is a bet on future margins in a price war with Swiggy/Zepto; the losses flag was a false alarm at the 2022 low, not proof the current price is safe. LESSON: judge loss-makers on unit economics (contribution margin, cohort retention) and on what dilution buys; recompute margins on a like-for-like revenue basis after model changes.

**Partly false alarm: Reliance's Jio-era debt doubling and ~10% ROCE** (`case_study:false-alarm-reliance-jio-debt`, verified). FLAGS: borrowings Rs 1.68 lakh cr (FY15) -> Rs 3.55 lakh cr (FY20); net debt Rs 1,61,035 cr (31 Mar 2020); ROCE stuck at 8-12% through FY15-26; Jio capex well ahead of revenue. CONTEXT: (1) the capex was ahead of demand that was very likely to come (India's mobile-data price elasticity) by a group with a cash-generating refining/petchem core and access to global capital; (2) Jio's price war drove the industry from many players to three, giving pricing power later; (3) leverage was cut by selling minority stakes at high valuations: Rs 1,15,694 cr from Jio Platforms investors (Facebook Rs 43,574 cr for 9.99%, Silver Lake, KKR, PIF etc.) plus a Rs 53,124 cr rights issue, and RIL declared itself net-debt-free on 19 Jun 2020. Stock: ~Rs 231 (2016) -> Rs 1,359 (Nov 2026), ~5.9x (~18% CAGR). HONEST VERDICT: the debt flag was a false alarm (no distress), but the low-ROCE flag stayed partly true: returns were good, not multibagger-grade, and the rights issue diluted holders who did not subscribe. LESSON: capex-ahead-of-demand is benign when demand is proven elsewhere, the sponsor can survive delays, and asset monetisation is possible; but low ROCE caps compounding.

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:TRANSRAILL:fy27-order-intake-10000cr`
- **Method:** promise-tracker credibility · **P(ours)** 0.38 · **P(base)** 0.50 · resolve by 2027-05-31
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (Nov-2026): order book ₹14,218 cr at 30-Sep-2026, plus ₹1,747 cr declared after quarter-end; MD Randeep Narang: 'confident to achieve an annual order intake of INR10,000-plus crores'; 'Already INR3,500 crores, INR4,000 crores in the bag'; ₹18,000 cr already bid + ~₹30,000 cr more to bid in 5 months at a 10–12% historical win ratio. 'Since listing, we have not missed any of our revenue or margin guidance' (revenue Q2 ₹2,056 cr, +32%; EBITDA margin 11.6%).
- **Why our number differs from base:** Arithmetic check: ₹48,000 cr of bids × 10–12% ≈ ₹4,800–5,800 cr more wins → ₹8,300–9,800 cr total, i.e., the target needs above-normal win rates. The clean record is on revenue/margin, not order intake (more lumpy). Lean below base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Indian EPC order-intake guidance with ~40% done at H1 is met roughly half the time.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if Transrail reports FY27 order intake/inflow (incl. L1 converted to orders within FY27, as the company counts it) ≥₹10,000 cr in its Q4 FY27 presentation, press release or call.
- **Resolution source:** Transrail Q4 FY27 investor presentation / earnings call transcript
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/TRANSRAIL_11112026120533_EarningcallTranscriptUFRSept2026.pdf

body:
- **promise-tracker credibility** — management stated a number or a date; we judge delivery from their track record and how much of the
  promise is already in the bag. A good method should beat the base rate most when it *disagrees* with management.
- **base rate** — we mostly lean on a reference class (seasonality, how often LoIs become binding, guidance-raise frequency) and move
  only a little for company specifics. If these calls score no better than the base column, that is expected and fine.
- **flags-judgment context** — a red flag is present (pledge, restatement, material weakness, going-concern doubt, missed coupon).
  The test (lesson L10/L12) is whether we can tell which flags have teeth for the specific event named.
- **sector cycle/lead indicator** — we use an observable lead indicator (QTD commodity prices, monthly exchange volumes, rate cycle,
  credit-cost trajectory) to forecast a next-quarter number.
- **valuation-temperature** — a stock is hot or cold versus its own history; we forecast 7-month relative price performance. The base
  rate is "a single stock beats its index a bit under half the time". Expect noise; only many such calls can show skill.
- **management-tone-vs-delivery** — management's words are noticeably more (or less) confident than the numbers; we bet on the gap.

title: batch2 › Method notes (what each call is testing)

body:
- ★ **Universe:** every symbol in the current NSE equity list (`EQUITY_L.csv`, EQ/BE) **listed on or before
  2023-12-31** (1,870 symbols), not a sample. The SUE-history requirement removes late listers anyway. Pre-filter:
  drop a symbol only if shares (latest filing) × unadjusted close never touches ₹400–60,000 cr in 2021–2026. Event-level
  filter ₹500–50,000 cr at entry, as in v1. Survivorship: current list only (same as v1). Delisted firms are absent and
  get the same audit logic as v1 §4.
- ★ **EPS basis:** for each event, **consolidated basic EPS** is used if the company filed consolidated results for the
  event quarter, the same quarter a year earlier, and at least 4 of the 8 prior seasonal-change pairs. All of those come
  from filings for quarters ended 30-Jun-2019 or later (FY2020+). Otherwise the event uses **standalone** EPS (v1
  basis). The SUE of an event never mixes bases. The basis is recorded per event, and the consolidated-only subset is
  reported as a sensitivity check (not a verdict).
- Consolidated EPS = basic EPS attributable to owners of the parent as tagged in the filing's XBRL (same tag priority as
  v1). Split/bonus adjustment as v1 D2. Returns are price returns (v1 D3).
- **Filings and dates:** quarters to Dec-2024 come from `corporates-financial-results`, and quarters from Dec-2024 on
  from `integrated-filing-results`. The union is used, with the earliest timestamp per quarter and basis. Event date is
  the earliest results announcement ("Financial Result Updates" / results "Outcome of Board Meeting") after
  quarter-end and no later than the feed date, else the feed date (v1 D8). ★ Announcements for symbols not in v1's
  cache come from NSE's all-company corporate-announcements feed queried one calendar day at a time. Filings more than
  150 days after quarter-end are dropped (v1 D5).
- Entry: adjusted close of the first NSE trading day strictly after the event date. Horizons: 21 / 63 / 126 days;
  **primary = 63**.
- **SUE:** as v1: `(EPS_q − EPS_{q−4}) / sd(previous up to 8 seasonal changes)`, with ≥ 4 prior changes required and
  sd > 0. Quintiles within each fiscal quarter (≥ 25 events). Tertiles by mcap within each fiscal quarter.
- **Controls:** as v1. Equal-weight return over the identical window of all universe stocks with fetched shares and
  prices, mcap ×0.5–×2 of the event firm on the entry date, firm itself excluded, ≥ 5 required. Excess = event return
  − control return.
- **Costs:** a long-only position pays one round trip: **net = excess − 1.0%** (also shown at 0.5%).
- **Fetch order and stopping rule (★, written before fetching):** pass A fetches, for every universe symbol in v1's
  seeded order (seed 20261121; then the 79 symbols listed in H2-2023, in alphabetical order), both filing lists and the
  XBRL for quarters ended **Dec-2022 → Sep-2026**. That is all the fresh test needs. Pass B then fetches quarters
  **Jun-2019 → Sep-2022** in the same order, for the 2022–25 re-run. If pass B cannot finish within this session's
  fetch budget, the re-run uses the symbols pass B completed. That subset is random by construction, and the report
  says so. No result statistic is computed before pass A is complete for every symbol.

body:
Already known from published results: the event-level 12-month halving rates of groups A–D in the combined-avoid
test (A 17.6%, B 8.3%, C 15.1%, D 6.1%; quarter bootstrap). Those pooled numbers already imply that, on all
events, red-flag vs no-flag halving is about 2.3×. **So the event-sample halving ratio below is a re-estimate, not a
blind test.** What is new and not yet computed: (1) the ratio for the *card's* trigger (pledge > 25% ∨ interest
cover < 1.5x, without S5) with financials excluded; (2) **firm-cluster** bootstrap CIs (the earlier test flagged its
halving CIs as too narrow because the same firm repeats across quarters); (3) 1-year and 3-year excess returns vs
size-matched controls; (4) 3-year failure; (5) the winner cost; (6) an **independent replication** on the
survivorship-free 2016/2018 snapshot panel (solvency + hard-filter v2 panel), where no halving or excess-return
comparison by this flag combination has been run (only 5-year failure lifts by single flag, L27/L28).
